newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones says Markets unit Q2 profit fades.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones says Markets unit Q2 profit fades.

text.p: Dow Jones & Co said Wednesday that second quarter profit fell nearly 33 percent over a year ago, with its troubled financial information unit hardly breaking even.

Operating profit at the financial information services segment, which includes Dow Jones Markets, Newswires and Global Indexes, fell nearly 100 percent in the second quarter to barely break-even of $169,000, compared to $40.3 million a year ago. Revenues dipped 4.5 percent.
Dow Jones said total quarterly earnings dropped to $34.9 million, or $0.36 per share, versus $52 million, or $0.54.

Dow Jones Chairman and Chief Executive Peter Kann said: "While the results at our Dow Jones Markets unit continue to adversely affect earnings, our plan for reinvigorating that unit remains right on track."

Dow Jones announced in January that it planned to invest as much as $650 million over the next three years to strengthen the unit, formerly known as Telerate. Some Wall Street money managers who have taken sizable stock positions in the company, including Michael Price, have pushed the company to sell or spin off the unit.
Kann said at the shareholders meeting in April that the company had considered a sale of the unit, a merger, or shrinking the size of the business before deciding to make the major investment.
Operating income fell about 15 percent in the second quarter to $78 million, while revenues rose nearly two percent to $641 million.
Operating income at its business publishing segment, which includes the results of its print publications and television operations, rose 54 percent to about $68.1 million.
Advertising linage at The Wall Street Journal newspaper rose 8.3 percent in the quarter.
